Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

This is the no-Bookshelf ablation: no cross-domain fish-control research shelf
is provided. Base controller proposals only on the task contract, current and
inherited guidance, sampled solver results, inherited optimizer logs, and
current rollout evidence. Do not search for or reconstruct the omitted shelf
from neighboring configurations or repository history.

I’m using the `read-wake-visual-signals-first` skill because this is a multi-wake target-policy change. I’ll read its full instructions and `README.md`, then inspect the current rollout evidence before touching the solver.

The only sampled rollout is the deliberately naive seed, so it serves as both the parent baseline and the informative failure; there is no positive finite comparator in this workspace. I’m now inspecting the shared prewarm and release-to-exit keyframes, then I’ll cross-check the frame-level metrics and diagnostics before writing the required diagnosis.

The evidence points to two concrete deficits: target blindness and actuator-saturated cadence. The fish briefly closes to 8.61 L, then rotates into a steep downward path and exits after 50.13 time units; its −13.30 L vertical displacement, near-zero relative-flow mean, exact velocity/acceleration cap hits, and 32.83 tailbeat-to-shedding ratio agree with the keyframes. I’m recording that diagnosis and a bounded bearing/velocity/moment steering hypothesis before changing the candidate, as required by the visual-first skill.

The candidate now keeps one state-encoded oscillator but slows it from 0.55 to 1.1, reduces bend amplitude, and adds bounded body-frame steering. I also added the durable negative lesson: the seed’s saturated high-cadence gait should not be treated as a useful propulsion baseline until yaw retention and actuator clipping are fixed. Next I’m validating the parameter schema and invoking the workspace’s required check runner; I will not run CFD.

The first required check found a workspace-rendering defect: `README.md` lists the same assigned guidance parent twice, so the checker sees two “copied to guidance/” entries even though both point to one identical parent. I’m inspecting the checker and parent hashes to repair this minimally without altering any evidence or solver scope.

The guidance check now passes after removing the duplicated parent entry. The policy check itself did not run because `julia` is absent from the shell `PATH` (exit 127), so I’m locating the workspace/runtime Julia binary and will rerun the exact non-CFD assertion with that executable.
